The **C9 League** (九校联盟) is an inter-university seminar composed of nine public universities in China. It was established on May 4, 1998 at the 100th anniversary of Peking University. 




## Membership[edit]


The C9 league comprises nine public universities:[1]

* University of Science and Technology of China – Hefei, Anhui
* Xi'an Jiaotong University – Xi'an, Shaanxi
* Zhejiang University – Hangzhou, Zhejiang

### World War II (1927–1949)[edit]


After the outbreak of the Second Sino-Japanese War in 1937 and the resulting expansion of Japanese territorial control in east China, Peking University was relocated to the southwestern city of Changsha and formed the Changsha Temporary University along with nearby schools Tsinghua University and Nankai University. In 1938, the three schools moved again, this time further southwest to Kunming, and formed the National Southwestern Associated University.

**C9 League (China’s “Ivy League”) – Member Universities and Their Founding Years**

| # | University (English) | Chinese Name | City / Province | Year Founded* |
|---|-----------------------|--------------|-----------------|---------------|
| 1 | **Peking University** | 北京大学 | Beijing | **1898** (Imperial University of Peking) |
| 2 | **Tsinghua University** | 清华大学 | Beijing | **1911** (originally Tsinghua College) |
| 3 | **Fudan University** | 复旦大学 | Shanghai | **1905** (Fudan Public School) |
| 4 | **Shanghai Jiao‑Tong University** | 上海交通大学 | Shanghai | **1896** (Nanyang Public School) |
| 5 | **Zhejiang University** | 浙江大学 | Hangzhou, Zhejiang | **1897** (Qiushi Academy) |
| 6 | **Nanjing University** | 南京大学 | Nanjing, Jiangsu | **1902** (Sanjiang Normal School → Nanking Higher Normal School) |
| 7 | **University of Science and Technology of China (USTC)** | 中国科学技术大学 | Hefei, Anhui | **1958** (established by the Chinese Academy of Sciences) |
| 8 | **Harbin Institute of Technology (HIT)** | 哈尔滨工业大学 | Harbin, Heilongjiang | **1920** (Harbin Sino‑Russian Industrial School) |
| 9 | **Xi’an Jia‑Tong University** | 西安交通大学 | Xi’an, Shaanxi | **1896** (Northern Jiaotong University, originally Imperial Railway College) |

\*The “founding year” reflects the earliest institutional origin that the university itself recognises as its establishment date (most are the year the predecessor school was created).  

---

### Quick Context

- **C9 League** is an alliance of China’s nine most elite public research universities, created on **4 May 1998** (the 100‑year anniversary of Peking University).  
- All nine members were originally part of **Project 985** and **Project 211**, flagship Chinese government programmes aimed at building world‑class universities.  
- The league functions as a platform for joint research, academic exchange, and policy dialogue among the top Chinese institutions, often being referred to as the “Chinese Ivy League.”

---

- **C9 League** – list of members.  
- Individual university pages for founding dates (e.g., “Peking University – founded 1898”, “Tsinghua University – founded 1911”, “Fudan University – founded 1905”, etc.).
